correctness.rationale: Independent endpoint-disjoint enumeration gave 24 allowed graph edges and augmented face counts (1,24,156,272,60). The stated priority toggles produced 217 disjoint Hasse pairs and exactly 79 unmatched three-edge faces. Topological elimination exhausted all 513 faces and all 1392 directed augmented cover relations. Restricting to the ordinary nonempty face poset discards the empty-face pair and retains a DAG (512 faces, 1368 arcs), with exactly one critical vertex and 79 critical 2-cells and no other critical cells. The discrete Morse CW model therefore attaches all 2-disks by their boundaries to the single vertex, giving a wedge of 79 two-spheres and the stated integral homology. The Euler characteristic 80 is a check, not the homotopy argument.
residual_risks: The exact matching pertains to this fixed eight-vertex graph; no extrapolation to cocktail-party graphs of other sizes or to equivariant homotopy is supported.

evidence: The outerplanar theorem does not apply: this graph has 24 edges, above 2·8−3=13.
The complete-graph theorem applies before deleting any edge; the same-date low-fault Resultary entry is explicitly limited to at most three deleted edges.
Full classification of general complete multipartite matching complexes was not established by the inspected sources.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Four disjoint deletions on eight vertices are outside all those hypotheses. In particular the three-fault boundary cannot be iterated without a separate gluing or Morse argument.

evidence: M(K₈) is already a wedge of 132 two-spheres; the audited matching complex is the induced subcomplex obtained by deleting four of its vertices.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The homotopy type of a complex does not determine that of a specified induced subcomplex. The Euler characteristic alone cannot establish simple connectivity or concentration in degree 2. The 79-sphere conclusion needs the additional topology supplied by the Morse certificate.

value.rationale: Deleting a whole perfect matching is a canonical symmetric boundary case, not an arbitrary graph-census entry. A complete homotopy comparison with intact K₈ shows the same sphere dimension and an exact fall from 132 to 79 summands after all four pair deletions. The finite certificate gives more than a change in Euler characteristic or field Betti numbers.
residual_risks: One finite deletion comparison; no monotonicity or general deletion-stability inference.
